### Conclusion
Your understanding is correct: current clinical evidence does not support the claim that ivermectin lowers the risk of death or severe outcomes from COVID-19.

### Key Evidence
* **Lack of Clinical Efficacy:** According to evaluations by health authorities like the U.S. FDA, available clinical trial data do not demonstrate that ivermectin is effective against COVID-19 in humans (https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html; https://www.webmd.com/drugs/what-is-ivermectin).
* **Major Randomized Trials:** Large clinical trials, such as the TOGETHER trial, found that ivermectin did not significantly reduce hospital admissions or disease progression among early-diagnosed COVID-19 outpatients (https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html).
* **No Reasonable Expectation of Benefit:** Evidence reviews conducted by health organizations conclude that there is no reasonable expectation of benefit when using ivermectin for COVID-19, and prescribing it outside of approved uses may pose safety risks (https://www.albertahealthservices.ca/assets/info/ppih/if-ppih-covid-19-sag-ivermectin-in-treatment-and-prevention-rapid-review.pdf).
* **Methodological Limitations in Positive Claims:** Systematic reviews examining early studies that claimed ivermectin was beneficial found that those reported benefits were primarily driven by methodological limitations and high risk of bias in the individual trials (https://www.academia.edu/97871966/Bias_as_a_source_of_inconsistency_in_ivermectin_trials_for_COVID_19_A_systematic_review_Ivermectins_suggested_benefits_are_mainly_based_on_potentially_biased_results).
